question: The price of sugar increased by 22.5%. Anita wants to keep her expenditure on sugar same as before. By what percentage must she reduce her consumption of sugar (correct to two place of decimals)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When expenditure is constant, reduction % in consumption = [R / (100 + R)] × 100

Given R = 22.5%

Reduction % = [22.5 / (100 + 22.5)] × 100

Reduction % = (22.5 / 122.5) × 100 = (9 / 49) × 100

Reduction % = 900 / 49 ≈ 18.37%

**∴ The correct answer is 18.37%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Price increase = 22.5%

Expenditure remains the same.

**Formula Used:**

Expenditure = Price × Consumption
